recommendation: Keep this focused source fix. It completes the FHIR-25289/FHIR-23710 wording application without changing Timing constraints or taking up broader unresolved dosage-example questions.
issue_request: FHIR-25289 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and asked to remove stale Timing.repeat.dayOfWeek and Timing.repeat.timeOfDay comments that said frequency and period could not be used with those elements, preserving schedules such as twice a day on Mondays and 10:00 AM every other day after FHIR-12460.
initial_application: The R5 MnM commit 5cbc14c7d0f361941099bf72066b75c3f74f6d4f mentioned FHIR-25289 and FHIR-23710, removed the explicit dayOfWeek frequency/period prohibition, and changed the timeOfDay mutual-exclusion text to only prohibit timeOfDay with when. It left the first timeOfDay sentence saying the action happens every day, which still conflicted with frequency/period combinations such as every other day.
additional_context: FHIR-23710 approved the timeOfDay comment text that only excludes when, and FHIR-12460 loosened Timing invariants so dayOfWeek/timeOfDay may be used with frequency and period. source/fhir.ini routes datatypes through the active datatypes build area, and source/datatypes/timing.xml is the authoritative Timing spreadsheet. Current dosage examples include period 2 days plus timeOfDay, confirming that current source expects timeOfDay to work with non-daily repeat timing.
reconciliation: Changed source/datatypes/timing.xml to say that when timeOfDay is specified, the action occurs at the specified time(s) as otherwise constrained by the repeat timing, while retaining the approved rule that timeOfDay and when are mutually exclusive.
source_changes: source/datatypes/timing.xml: updated the Timing.repeat.timeOfDay comment to remove the misleading unconditional daily inference and defer repetition semantics to the rest of Timing.repeat.

related_jiras.note: Loosened Timing invariants so dayOfWeek/timeOfDay can coexist with frequency and period.
Approved timeOfDay wording that only excludes when, and was historically applied with FHIR-25289.
Introduced the original timeOfDay comment wording that later became stale after the Timing invariant changes.
Unresolved R6 dosage-example issue includes current examples using timeOfDay with every-other-day timing; it was not a final decision for this reconciliation.
